item.title: Chinese VP attends COP31 Antalya Leaders' Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, as President Xi Jinping's special representative, attends the Antalya Leaders' Summit of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) and delivers a national statement, in Antalya, Türkiye, Nov. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing)
ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, as President Xi Jinping's special representative, attended the Antalya Leaders' Summit of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) on Wednesday and delivered a national statement.
Han said that Xi has pointed out that responding to climate change is the common cause of all humanity, adding that the adverse effects of global climate change are becoming increasingly apparent.
In light of the new circumstances, Han put forward a four-point proposal.
The first is to stay focused on common goals and strengthen collective action.
He called for the full and effective implementation of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement in accordance with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, so as to rally collective efforts in global climate governance.
Developed countries should take the lead in reducing emissions and fulfill their climate finance commitments, Han said, stressing that all parties should make every effort to implement their nationally determined contributions and strive to do better.
The second is to accelerate the green transition and promote low-carbon development.
Efforts should be made to facilitate the free flow of high-quality green technologies and products, and promote the transformation and upgrading of the economic and industrial structures, Han said.
Noting that China has set targets for 2030, including raising the share of non-fossil energy in total electricity generation to 50 percent and increasing the share of electricity in final energy consumption to 35 percent, Han said that China remains firmly committed to achieving its carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals.
The third is to prevent climate-related disasters and enhance climate resilience.
Equal importance should be attached to mitigation and adaptation, he said, adding that cooperation should be strengthened in areas such as disaster prevention and mitigation, monitoring and early warning, and disaster relief, so as to enhance climate adaptation capacity.
He noted that China is willing to promote the application of its intelligent meteorological early warning solution "MAZU" in more countries, helping them prevent and respond to climate risks.
The fourth is to adhere to openness and inclusiveness and deepen international cooperation.
He said that support and assistance to developing countries should be strengthened to jointly build a clean and beautiful world.
China has continued to promote South-South cooperation projects on climate change, such as the "Africa Solar Belt," and will launch the capacity-building project "Global South climate action leadership program," said the Chinese vice president, noting that China will also contribute to the fair and effective implementation of the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation.

item.title: Chinese VP meets Turkish president
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, as President Xi Jinping's special representative, meets with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on the sidelines of the Antalya Leaders' Summit of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Nov. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing)
ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, as President Xi Jinping's special representative, met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Antalya Leaders' Summit of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).
Conveying Xi's cordial greetings and best wishes to Erdogan, Han said that China and Türkiye enjoy a long history of friendly exchanges.
Under the strategic guidance of Xi and Erdogan, China-Türkiye relations have maintained sound and steady development, Han said, noting that China stands ready to work with Türkiye to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, deepen practical cooperation across various fields, and promote the continuous development of the China-Türkiye strategic cooperative relationship.
Noting that the two heads of state have reached an important political consensus on accommodating each other's core interests and major concerns, Han said the two sides should support each other in pursuing the paths chosen by their own people and safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests.
The two countries should elevate the level of practical cooperation, he said, stressing that China is ready to encourage more Chinese enterprises to invest and start businesses in Türkiye in line with market-oriented and commercial principles.
The two sides enjoy broad prospects for cooperation in renewable energy, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and other fields, and can jointly create more highlights in bilateral cooperation, Han added.
China appreciates Türkiye's efforts to advance global climate governance, and stands ready to work with Türkiye to ensure the success of COP31, the Chinese vice president said.
Erdogan, for his part, asked Han to convey his sincere greetings and best wishes to Xi.
He said that Türkiye attaches great importance to developing relations with China and firmly adheres to the one-China principle.
The Turkish president recalled that he met with Xi and reached a new consensus to promote the development of Türkiye-China relations at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Tianjin Summit last year.
Türkiye is willing to firmly promote the implementation of the consensus, maintain close high-level exchanges with China, advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, enhance trade and investment, expand cooperation in new energy, minerals, artificial intelligence, transportation, tourism and other fields, promote people-to-people exchanges, and elevate Türkiye-China relations to a new level, said Erdogan.
He noted that Türkiye appreciates China's important contributions to promoting world peace and development, and hopes to enhance communication and collaboration with China to jointly promote peace and stability in the Middle East and work together to address global challenges such as climate change.

item.title: Chinese FM holds positive, constructive phone talks with Rubio on China-U.S. ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday held positive and constructive phone talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The two sides had an in-depth exchange of views on China-U.S. relations and the interaction between the two heads of state.
During the talks, Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said that President Xi Jinping's visit to the United States in September was smooth and successful.
The two heads of state agreed to enrich the connotation of a new vision of China-U.S. relations, providing clearer strategic guidance for exploring a right approach for the two countries to get along with each other, Wang said.
The stable momentum of China-U.S. relations has not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on their respective and common interests, Wang said.
China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy towards the United States, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the U.S. side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results, Wang said.

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth.
Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925.
Addressing the event in the Great Hall of the People, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution.
Xi noted that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun.
For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said.
"The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said.

item.title: PLA Air Force marks 77th anniversary amid modernization drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
The Red Falcon aerobatics team from the Aviation University of Air Force performs during celebrations to mark the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force in Changchun, northeast China's Jilin Province, Nov. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Linyun)
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force marked its 77th founding anniversary on Wednesday, highlighting its journey from a modest beginning to a modernizing force with a structure geared toward future operational needs.
In an anniversary video, the Air Force, founded on Nov. 11, 1949, showcased training exercises involving fighter jets, bombers, early warning aircraft, transport planes, helicopters and drones, as well as ground-based air defense missile units, radar units and airborne troops.
The video, released Wednesday on the service's official social media accounts, also highlighted the Air Force's participation in disaster relief and international exchanges, drawing a wave of congratulatory messages.
Anniversary celebrations had begun earlier this month, with events held in different parts of the country.
On Monday morning, eight flight instructors from the Aviation University of the Air Force in Changchun, capital of northeast China's Jilin Province, took to the skies in jet trainers for an aerial display.
That evening, 3,000 drones lit up the sky in a light show depicting the Air Force's evolution, from horse-towed propeller-driven trainer aircraft, to advanced aircraft such as J-20 stealth fighter and Y-20 transport plane.
On Nov. 6, six J-10 jets from the PLA Air Force's Bayi (August 1) Aerobatic Team flew over the Great Wall in north China's Tianjin Municipality as part of the celebrations. The team derives its name from the founding anniversary of the PLA.
"The Great Wall was once a barrier against invaders," said Zha Xiufeng, one of the pilots. "Today, we pilots serve as an 'airborne Great Wall,' safeguarding the peace and security of countless families."
The PLA Air Force started with a small fleet of outdated aircraft. During the founding ceremony of the People's Republic of China on Oct. 1, 1949, only 17 aircraft were available for parade.
In the following years, the Air Force shot down or damaged more than 3,800 enemy aircraft, according to official figures. More than 1,800 Air Force personnel have given their lives in combat operations, scientific research tasks, and dedication to the interests of the people.
The PLA Air Force's three-step development roadmap, issued in 2018, set targets to build a strategic air force by 2020, basically establish a modernized strategic air force by 2035, and become a world-class air force by the middle of the century.
The 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, scheduled to run from Dec. 7 to 13 in Zhuhai, will offer the world a glimpse of the PLA Air Force's latest developments.
The Air Force said multiple types of its main combat equipment would make their debut at the show. Equipment for aerial reconnaissance, early warning, air defense, support, airborne operations, unmanned applications and intelligent systems, as well as munitions, will also be displayed at the exhibition.
"Bringing more domestically developed new-generation aircraft closer to the public and taking Air Force stories into households across the country are commitments we will continue to uphold," said Gao Xiang, a senior Air Force official.
As the PLA Air Force has developed, its international engagement has also expanded.
In 2026, the Bayi Aerobatic Team performed at the 10th Singapore Airshow, while a range of aircraft, including fighters, tankers, special-purpose aircraft and helicopters, took part in the China-Egypt "Eagles of Civilization 2026" joint air force training as an integrated force.
Moreover, Chinese and Russian air forces conducted a joint strategic patrol over the western Pacific and other airspace, demonstrating their resolve and capability to uphold regional peace and stability. Chinese and Belarusian airborne troops also held urban counterterrorism exercises in central China.
"We will continue to engage with our counterparts around the world, build mutual trust through interaction, deepen cooperation through exchanges, and work together to safeguard the shared airspace of humanity," Gao said.

item.title: American's decades-long bond with Chinese hometown leaves legacy of kindness
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
This file photo taken on Sept. 19, 2005 shows David V. Plymire in Huangyuan County, northwest China's Qinghai Province. (Xinhua)
XINING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- In 1987, when David V. Plymire first returned to Huangyuan, the plateau county in China he had left decades earlier for the United States, locals were surprised that he still spoke the local dialect fluently.
"I simply talked to myself in front of a mirror so that I wouldn't forget the dialect of my hometown," he later explained to a local journalist.
Born in 1931 in the United States, Plymire spent his formative years with his family in Huangyuan County, now in northwest China's Qinghai Province, before leaving at age 18. Now, the 95-year-old regards the county as his only hometown.
Though an ocean away, Plymire never stopped thinking about the people of Huangyuan. Between 1987 and 2016, he returned more than 20 times, helping improve local health care and education.
To support the once-underdeveloped county, he donated over 30 pieces of medical equipment worth some 6 million yuan (about 895,500 U.S. dollars) to the Huangyuan County People's Hospital.
The donation included a CT scanner worth 350,000 U.S. dollars -- a piece of equipment that no other county-level hospital in Qinghai possessed at the time. The procurement and customs clearance process for the large machine was cumbersome, and only after numerous setbacks did it finally arrive in Huangyuan in 2000.
Standing before the device, Plymire bowed deeply. "This scanner must serve the people of my hometown well," he said in the local dialect.
In 2002, Jia Chengwu, a neurosurgeon from Shenyang, capital of northeast China's Liaoning Province, was dispatched to Huangyuan as part of the country's efforts to promote large-scale development of the western region. There, he performed the county's first craniotomy on a migrant worker with a head injury.
"Without the CT scanner donated by Mr. Plymire, which enabled a timely diagnosis of the worker's intracranial hematoma, I could not have completed that surgery," Jia recalled. "With this batch of donated hardware and the paired assistance from supporting doctors, the hospital became a well-known medical institution in the surrounding area."
Huang Jiong, head of the hospital, said the CT scanner remained in service for 15 years until around 2015, benefiting more than 20,000 people.
The equipment allowed doctors to quickly diagnose hundreds of critically ill patients suffering from cerebral hemorrhage, cerebral infarction and meningitis, securing precious time for surgical rescue and saving numerous lives, Huang said.
In addition to donating medical equipment, Plymire also coordinated with foreign friends to teach English at local schools.
His sister, Mary Ann Plymire, who was born and grew up in Huangyuan, funded the purchase of the county's first ambulance.
In 1998, the Huangyuan county government awarded both of them honorary citizenship.
At Mary's request, her ashes were brought back to the county after she died in 2016, allowing her to rest in peace in the place where she spent her childhood.
The roots of their devotion trace back to their father, Victor G. Plymire, a missionary who arrived in China in 1908 and settled in Huangyuan in 1921.
According to David's book depicting his father's life in Huangyuan, the senior Plymire dedicated himself to treating villagers free of charge with modern medicine. He also sheltered locals from a warlord's massacre in a self-built gospel hall in 1929 and provided relief to refugees from Gansu and Shaanxi provinces in the 1940s during the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression.
"I believe the father and son are remembered not merely for the medical donations and educational assistance, but more importantly, because they sheltered the common people during an extremely special and life-threatening era," said Huo De, a cultural scholar at the county's federation of literary and art circles. "This is the foundation of the local people's deep affection for them."
Now, the hospital incorporates David's story into its orientation training for new employees and internal study sessions, keeping alive this legacy of cross-border goodwill.
"David did not simply donate a few pieces of equipment. He has become a moral role model," Huang said.
The example set by the Plymires has continued to inspire others to follow.
Influenced by Plymire, Jia, now 74 and retired for many years, overcomes altitude sickness to regularly visit Huangyuan at his own expense to lecture, see outpatients, and perform surgeries at the hospital. He has also sponsored three local students from Huangyuan and its neighboring area, including a Tibetan pupil.
"We should follow David's example and do more good deeds," said Jia.
This undated file photo shows David V. Plymire (C) and his sister Mary Ann Plymire (R) communicate with Yu Yaode, former director of Huangyuan County People's Hospital, at the hospital in Huangyuan County, northwest China's Qinghai Province. (Xinhua)
Wang Shikang (R), the former head of the Huangyuan County People's Hospital, Huang Jiong (C), the current head of the hospital, and Bai Qiming, son of David V. Plymire's childhood friend Bai Yongsheng, greet David V. Plymire during a video meeting on Nov. 2, 2026.

item.title: Beyond China's shopping festival: How Singles' Day shifts from local to global retail barometer
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
A drone photo taken on Nov. 11, 2026 shows an intelligent package sorting line in Xinghua City, east China's Jiangsu Province. (Photo by Zhou Shegen/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Nearly two decades after its launch, China's Singles' Day shopping festival has become an increasingly influential event in global retail. Overseas brands and e-commerce platforms are adjusting their promotional schedules, supply chains and product launches to tap into the Chinese market.
Also known as Double 11 because it falls on Nov. 11, the annual online shopping carnival is one of the world's largest retail events. This year's edition, which has run for nearly a month, is set to conclude, highlighting a shift toward a wider range of services, smarter AI shopping assistants and more vibrant two-way trade through cross-border commerce.
SERVICE CONSUMPTION AS A NEW ENGINE
During this year's event, major e-commerce platforms expanded their offerings beyond traditional consumer goods and discounts, giving greater prominence to services. JD.com showcased more than 100 service products for the first time, while Suning offered packages such as a 9.9-yuan (about 1.47 U.S. dollars) whole-house appliance inspection.
The trend reflects broader changes in China's consumer market, which is now driven by both goods and services. In the first three quarters of this year, service retail sales grew 4 percentage points faster than goods retail sales, making services a key source of incremental consumption.
A Beijing resident surnamed Feng said his Double 11 purchases included a two-day hotel package and a home cleaning card. "There are more and more services to choose from. Buying these packages on major platforms offers good value, and fulfillment and after-sales service are more reliable," he said.
Physical goods, however, remain a major part of the shopping festival. Sales of smartphones covered by government trade-in subsidies on Tmall surged more than ninefold, while transactions in categories such as maternal and infant products and home appliances on Taobao's on-demand retail platform grew more than 70 percent year on year.
Combined sales on China's major integrated e-commerce platforms during the early phase of this year's Singles' Day reached 1.0263 trillion yuan as of Oct. 31, data firm Syntun showed. This year, the Tmall Double 11 event featured 1 million global brands and 72 million products in promotion. That contrasts sharply with the first edition in 2009, when only 27 brands took part and transactions totaled 52 million yuan.
AI ELEMENTS
One notable development this year was the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) tokens as an independent product category on multiple e-commerce platforms, a sign that AI is rapidly integrating into every link of the e-commerce chain.
Taobao, Douyin and Pinduoduo all embedded smarter AI shopping functions during this year's Double 11. Last year, Taobao and JD.com introduced AI shopping guides that could answer product questions and search by photo.
This year, many platforms rolled out conversational AI shopping assistants for the first time -- tools that can sort shopping carts, automatically calculate combined discounts and subsidies, and handle after-sales follow-up.
Li Mingtao, chief e-commerce expert at the China International Electronic Commerce Center, said consumers' use of AI shopping assistants has moved from trial to large-scale adoption, and the expanding functions mark a shift from tools to intelligent agents.
"In previous years, consumers spent considerable time hunting for coupons and comparing prices. AI shopping assistants take on that time burden, turning complex promotional rules into clear, actionable shopping plans," Li said.
AI is also changing how online retailers operate, improving efficiency and streamlining operations. Alibaba's QwenWork launched an e-commerce version ahead of Singles' Day, while JD.com upgraded its AI business center to provide merchants with dozens of tools covering product selection, operations, fulfillment and after-sales.
GLOBAL RESONANCE
The festival's influence is increasingly extending beyond China. With the rise of global digital consumption and improving cross-border e-commerce policies, many platforms and merchants looked overseas for new growth during this year's event, while international brands are leveraging China's Singles' Day to expand market share.
This year, Taobao opened a one-click overseas channel for the first time, allowing merchants to sell in both domestic and overseas markets with their existing stores and products. AliExpress's official warehouses covered six countries, with pre-event overseas warehouse inventory up 146 percent year on year.
"Going overseas is not simply about selling goods abroad," said Sun Yanyan, head of Sparkone Media, a cross-border e-commerce company. "It is about exporting China's mature digital retail, supply chain and AI operations capabilities, building a two-way channel that helps transform Chinese manufacturing into Chinese brands and better connects domestic and international markets."
While platforms expand overseas, quality imported goods continue to enrich choices for Chinese consumers. A Shanghai resident surnamed Liu bought Australian infant food and Belgian nutritional supplements on Tmall Global during Singles' Day.
"In the past, many overseas local brands were hard to buy," she said. "Now the platform has sufficient bonded warehouse stock and fast customs clearance and delivery, so I can shop for specialty goods from around the world without traveling abroad."
Currently, imported food products on the Taobao and Tmall platforms cover more than 100 countries, over 1,000 production regions, and more than one million items.
This year, the Singles' Day festival coincided with the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), held in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10. The expo attracted 4,142 overseas companies from 162 countries, regions and international organizations, with more than 480 representative new products making their debuts.
Many of these products were not merely on display -- they were simultaneously listed on Singles' Day platforms, shortening the distance between global innovation and Chinese consumers. At the Tmall Global booth, AI-related gadgets were among the highlights: Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses, Oura smart rings and Fitbit Air wristbands were launched simultaneously at the CIIE and on Singles' Day.
According to Tmall Global, more than 1,800 new brands opened stores on the platform over the past year, and 1,300-plus imported brands participated in Singles' Day for the first time.
To address information gaps in cross-border shopping, Tmall Global launched a "Global Traceability Program" in May this year. More than 50 global brands have joined, and more than half of participating brands recorded double-digit year-on-year sales growth during this year's Singles' Day.
Besides Taobao and Tmall, other Chinese platforms such as Temu, Shein and TikTok Shop have brought Double 11 promotions to dozens of countries, while some Western retailers have adjusted their year-end promotional calendars in response.
Eighteen years on, Singles' Day no longer belongs to one country or one platform. From promotional calendars and logistics to product categories and consumer trust, it has become a global retail landmark -- and for many, an increasingly important indicator of changes in China's consumer market and of how the country continues to innovate and open up.

item.title: China holds gathering to mark 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
A gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Ding Haitao)
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China on Thursday held a gathering in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addressed the gathering.
Also present at the event were Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee.
More than a century ago, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. He died in 1925.

item.title: How China is rebuilding 3,000-year-old bronze treasures
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
How do you put ancient treasures back together after thousands of years? At China's Sanxingdui archaeological site, conservators combine meticulous hands-on restoration with 3D scanning and digital modeling to study broken bronze artifacts and help reveal the extraordinary craftsmanship of ancient Shu civilization.
